itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road typically opens in late spring and Cache Col holds consolidated snow well into summer, so most parties do this in July-September when the col crossing is firm but not icy.

days.note: Hike the maintained Cascade Pass Trail to Cascade Pass, then leave the trail and climb cross-country over the Cache Glacier remnant to Cache Col before dropping about a mile to camp at Kool-Aid Lake, a small tarn at ~6,320 ft. This stretch is mostly on snow into midsummer and is the crux of the day more from routefinding/snow travel than distance.
days.title: Approach to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Reach high camp below the Magic Mountain-Hurry-Up col

days.note: An early start lets you climb the peak on firm snow before it softens: ascend about 1,000 ft from camp to the Magic-Hurry-Up col, then follow the south ridge over a false summit to the true 7,821 ft top. Back at camp by mid-morning, most parties break camp and hike all the way out the same day rather than adding a third night.
days.title: Climb Hurry-Up Peak, then hike out

schedule.label: Leave Kool-Aid Lake camp
schedule.detail: Early start for firm snow on the col approach.

schedule.label: Summit via the south ridge
schedule.detail: Scramble past a false summit to the true 7,821 ft top.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break camp, filter water, repack for the hike out.

schedule.label: Begin the hike out
schedule.detail: Re-cross Cache Col and descend past Cascade Pass.

schedule.label: Back at the trailhead
schedule.detail: Roughly 3,000 ft of net descent from camp to the car.

days.objective: Tag the summit via the South Ridge and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night trip: about 16 miles round trip with roughly 4,800 ft of total gain, mostly spent covering the Cascade Pass-Cache Col approach rather than the short summit scramble itself.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong off-trail/cross-country fitness for the approach into a basin camp near Horseshoe Basin/Sahale-Boston country, plus a full scramble day on summit day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight pack (camp gear + basic scramble kit) on the approach; lighter day pack for the summit push

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day trip: roughly a full day off-trail to establish camp in Horseshoe Basin, then about 5 hrs round trip from camp to the summit via the south ridge
requiredSkills: Steep snow travel and self-arrest for lingering early-season snow patches
Comfortable with sustained exposure and no fixed protection
Basic wilderness/self-rescue judgment given the remote location
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced scrambler comfortable with sustained, unroped Class 3-4 terrain on loose rock; given the remote, low-traffic setting, prior North Cascades alpine scrambling experience and solid self-rescue judgment are strongly recommended

pro_tips: Pair with Sahale or a Horseshoe Basin tour
Catch firm morning snow on the approach

itinerary.cal: South Face is typically climbed August-September once snow clears the loose rock; overnight camps fall inside the North Cascades NP Complex/Ross Lake NRA backcountry, which requires a wilderness camping permit.

days.note: From the Canyon Creek Trailhead, hike FST 738 through McMillan Park to Crater Lake, then climb to the Crater Mountain saddle, cross/skirt the Jerry Glacier basin, and descend scree and heather to a camp near Crater Creek or the Jerry Lakes basin. This is the long day of the trip, mostly off-trail after the saddle.
days.title: Approach to high camp

schedule.label: Top out at Crater Mountain saddle
Reach camp near Crater Creek Meadows/Jerry Lakes

days.objective: Reach a high camp near Crater Creek Meadows / Jerry Lakes basin (~6,000-6,200 ft)

days.note: Climb from camp up to the ~7,200 ft step in the Southeast Ridge, then pick through loose class 3-4 terrain on the South Face (past the fish-shaped snowfield and hidden chimney) back onto the ridge crest to the summit. Reverse the route to camp; many parties then shuttle gear partway toward the Jerry Lakes saddle in the evening to shorten the exit day.
days.title: Summit day: South Face / SE Ridge

schedule.label: Optional camp shuffle
schedule.detail: Some parties relocate toward the Jerry Lakes/6,550 ft saddle to shorten Day 3

days.objective: Climb Jack Mountain (9,069 ft) via the South Face and Southeast Ridge, then reposition camp

days.note: Retrace the approach back over the Jerry Lakes/Crater Mountain saddle area (some parties detour past the East Crater Mountain lookout site) and descend to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

schedule.label: Pass Crater Mountain saddle / lookout area

days.objective: Return to the Canyon Creek Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~22-24 mile round trip with roughly 11,000-11,500 ft of cumulative gain: one long day to a ~6,000-6,200 ft high camp, one long summit day up the loose South Face/SE Ridge (~9-9.5 hrs camp-to-camp), and one day to hike out.

access.fees: $10 per person NPS backcountry camping fee (Ross Lake NRA/NOCA) plus a $6 non-refundable reservation fee if booked in advance; no fee for the USFS Pasayten Wilderness permit.
access.notes: 60% of sites (Boston Basin/Eldorado/Sulphide Glacier/etc.) are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (12 in on-trail corridors). Boston Basin camping restricted to two designated sites (Low Camp ~5,300 ft, High Camp ~6,400 ft). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.
access.permit: Free self-issue Pasayten Wilderness permit at the Canyon Creek Trailhead for the USFS approach. If camping within the North Cascades National Park Complex/Ross Lake NRA boundary, an NPS backcountry permit is required, available via Recreation.gov (advance reservation) or first-come/first-served at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.closures: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) closes for winter roughly between Ross Dam TH (MP134) and Silver Star Gate (MP171), typically early December through mid-April/May depending on snowpack — the Canyon Creek Trailhead is unreachable during that closure. Check WSDOT's North Cascades Highway pass report before planning a trip.
access.landManager: Approach trails (Canyon Creek TH, Jackita Ridge Trail #738/#746, Crater Lake) are in Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District, within the Pasayten Wilderness; the peak and upper basins sit on/near the boundary with the Ross Lake National Recreation Area (North Cascades National Park Complex, NPS).
access.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades National Park Complex backcountry permit (covers Ross Lake NRA) - quota, not free
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, or get a walk-up permit at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount. Cross-country climbing camps need a permit for the zone you camp in.
